steps.text: Place ground beef in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble, and set aside.

Place a the potatoes in a layer to cover the bottom of the slow cooker. Sprinkle the celery over the potatoes, and cover with a layer of ground beef. Season each layer with salt and pepper. Throw in the carrots, onions and peas. Mix together the tomato soup and water, and pour over the top. Cover, and set to low for 6 to 8 hours.

review.reviewBody: Before trying out a recipe, I always read the reviews. I took the advice of a couple other reviews and did the following: used corn instead of peas, used 3 cups of water instead of 1 1/4, used 3 boullion cubes and added one can diced tomatoes. It was wonderful and easy! I will make this again!

This recipe is a staple in my meal rotation. I follow the recipe exactly as written. Except I have a salt intolerance so omit that. I do add extra veggies if I make it in the summer (to take camping). Especially, if I have an abundance of garden veggies. I have added extra: fresh tomatoes, beans, corn, peas, and herbs from my garden. If I make this recipe in the winter I will add extra potatoes, carrots and no/low salt tomato soup to make it heartier. This soup also freezes well in a Mason/Kerr jar and tastes just as awesome thawed and reheated. (I do this for my camping soup. Put it frozen in the cooler as an ice block. When it has thawed sufficiently I heat it in a Dutch Oven over coals and serve it with cornbread) I actually crave this when I am not feeling well. I will make a big slow cooker pot full, and sip on it for a couple days. Thanks for the recipe.

This looks more like a stew than a soup. I make this kind of soup much easier. I use canned puree tomatoes, olive oil, 1 onion and garlic diced , thyme, parsley, garlic powder, chicken broth, penne pasta, half a bag of mixed veggies, premade frozen meatballs, salt, pepper and sugar. I pour 2 Tbsp of olive oil in a dutch oven, saute the diced onion and garlic, thyme and add canned tomatoes some water and simmer for a few, add sugar, then broth. Bring it all to a boil then add remaining ingredients, simmer for 10-15 minutes until pasta is done and meatballs are heated through

Very very bland for our family’s taste buds. We’re used to soups being very flavorful and full bodied. However, upon making it adding in all the ingredients, plus my own spices, my kids walking past said how great it smelled and they couldn’t wait to try it! I used leftover taco meat plus added more ground beef. We like more meat in our soups. I didn’t leave out the peas and they were very tasty in this soup. I did add beef bouillon and more water than it called for. All my veggies were as stated but fresh in the recipe plus a few potatoes. I also didn’t add tomatoes. Just our preference. Made in this in my instant pot and it took longer to cut up all the fresh veggies than it did to cook. Def will make again when weather becomes more brisk. Thanks for the recipe.

I added extra spices: fresh basil, celery salt, 2 bouillon cubes. When I cooked the meat I added ground nutmeg. I would suggest a few more potatoes and more water. I also added a can of Italian seasoned diced tomatoes. When serving I put fresh grated Parmesan cheese on top.

I didn't have time for the slow cooker, so I made it stove top in a kettle. I started with the onion, then added potatoes to allow for the most cooking time. I browned the ground beef before adding, and substituted spaghetti sauce instead of tomato sauce. It was ready in under an hour. Served with a little cheese on top, and drop biscuits on the side- yummy!

Delish. I made this stove top basically following the recipe. Except I added spices, marjoram and Sunny Spain Seasoning, and I used left over meatloaf adding it after the vegetables were cooked. Also sautéed mushrooms and onions together and added them with the meatloaf.

This was just okay. There are so many versions of Hamburger soup. I like my version much better. I don't use tomato soup . I use 2 cans tomato sauce and 1 can diced tomatoes with green chilis. For the frozen veggies I use 1 pkg. of veg. soup mix and 1 frozen mixed veg. I also add diced potatoes. I season the meat with salt, pepper and lots of garlic powder. The onion is cooked with the meat. Then the rest is added and cooked till the veg. are done.

Ok...a 4-ish before a few additions. Certainly has potential to be 5! I made a few small changes in the beginning...I didn't have large potatoes, I had small yukon golds, so I just added enough to look like 2 large (lol)...and I cubed them. I diced the onions instead of slicing them because it's easier to get my kids to eat them that way. I also used corn instead of peas, beef broth instead of water, added a can of diced tomatoes, and lots of garlic. I cooked it in the crock on low for about 8 hours. Tasted it. It was pretty bland. I added more beef bouillion granules, more fresh ground pepper, about 1/2 tsp. Italian seasoning, and a couple small pinches of cayenne. Oh, and more garlic. Put the crockpot on warm and let it "stew" until my bread was finished (about 40 minutes). The end result was AWESOME! My kids and hubby were eating like uncivilized heathens! I had to remind the girls a couple of times to use their table manners. It was that good! I'm definitely adding the recipe with changes to my rotation! Thanks!

3 1/2 so I rounded up. It would be five stars with the changes I made. With the changes, I loved it and so did my husband. I added a diced yellow bell pepper just to get rid of it, can of diced tomatoes, and two beef boulion to the water before mixing it with the tomato sauce. In between layers of veggies, I added generous amounts of seasoning: Salt, pepper, garlic salt, onion powder, sweet basil, thyme, and seasoned salt. This is a good base recipe, just ad more seasonings and it is great.

Delicious soup! I had 2 pounds of hamburger so decided to use it all and adjusted the recipe to work for me. I used 4 medium potatoes, 2 medium onions, skipped the celery and added a 6 oz. can of green chilis (medium heat) for a little zip. I also added 8 oz. of baby carrots and a 16 oz. bag of frozen corn along with 2 cans tomato soup, 1 can tomato sauce, 1 can diced tomatoes and a 32 oz. carton of beef broth. Husband loved it!
Added petite potatoes!
Added 4 cups beef broth instead of water, diced tomatoes, fresh garlic and Montreal steak seasoning to my meat. Served with egg noodles, and it’s yummy! My kids love it!
I substituted V8 juice for water and tomato soup. It was awesome!!! My kids wanted seconds and my husband (not a soup lover) really liked it and said "I'd eat that again". 😁
Have been making this for years, My family loves it and it's so easy to make.
Added a package of Beefy Onion Lipton soup mix to the water and tomato soup. This was a crowd-pleaser! Will definitely be making it again.
I substituted beef broth for the water and added a bit of HP sauce. delicious!
Great soup, loved it. Soup was as much of a stew as a soup.

Added 16oz bag of mixed vegetables, garlic powder and onion powder. Used large can 28oz Italian seasoned diced tomatoes and 3 cups water with 3tsp beef bouillon powder instead of tomato soup and water.
